findings.place: section 4.4, test 1 (a) 'startStand with a counting deps.spawn'; section 14, sub-step 1, own check (b) 'a counting deps.spawn'; section 16, 'R2 rule for every series'; section 1 lead-in and F29 ('Every Pixel Office server and every hook of every trial had SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR and HOME under the temporary root'); section 15 R2 'by construction'
findings.what: R2 is claimed to hold by construction, but the design does not require that a call which is given the owner's real home folder or real state folder can never start a process. A 'counting' spawn may be a real spawn (the counter of E2S-05 is one), so a regression or a mutant of rule P turns the refusal case of 'isolated start', and the developer's own check (b), into a start of Pixel Office on the owner's real folder (a start row in the real server-starts.jsonl, the real port and node-path files replaced). The series rule of section 16 covers product mutants that write into a home and starter mutants with the stand-in, but not mutants of the spec's own checks. This already happened in the design's own trial: the prototype calls runHook for the real folder with no injected spawn (<scratch>/e2e106-01/proto/tools/test/e2e/pixel-office.e2e.js line 180, against the design's own words 'its injected spawn not called'), and the mutant R02 (<scratch>/e2e106-01/sk/mut_product.py line 45, output mut_product.out line 29 'Missing expected rejection.' in 0.2 s) ran the real hook program with SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR = the owner's real state folder and HOME = the temporary root. The hook read the real write-secret and port file; it wrote nothing only because no owner server was listening. With the owner's Pixel Office running, the same run signs with the real secret and appends an invented event to the owner's journal.
findings.needed: (1) In 4.4 test 1 (a) and in 14 own check (b): every call that is given the real home folder or the real state folder - startStand and runHook alike - passes a deps.spawn that records the call and throws, never a real spawn, written as a rule with its reason. (2) In section 16, the R2 rule: a mutant that removes or weakens a check of rule P or of runHook is run only where that throwing seam stands. (3) The sentence of F29 / section 1 and of the step-01 self_check corrected for R02 (issue I1). Measured on my sketch: with the throwing seam the same R02 mutant is red in 'isolated start' and starts no process.

findings.place: section 4.1, rule P, step (3) 'passed through assertOutsideRepo'; section 11.1, E2S-03; section 16, S05-S11
findings.what: No test and no mutant pins the third step of rule P. issues.text: The step-01 handoff (self_check.real_state_folder_after) and design section 1 / F29 say that every Pixel Office server and every hook of every trial had SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR and HOME under the temporary root. That does not hold for the author's mutant R02: <scratch>/e2e106-01/sk/mut_product.py line 45 removes the folder checks of the prototype's runHook, and the prototype's refusal case (<scratch>/e2e106-01/proto/tools/test/e2e/pixel-office.e2e.js line 180) passes the real state folder with no injected spawn, so the real hook program ran with SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR = the owner's real folder (mut_product.out line 29: 'Missing expected rejection.', 0.2 s). The real folder's hash stayed the same (the designer's, ORCH's and my readings agree) because no owner server was listening. This is the evidence of F1; ORCH decides whether it also goes into docs/anti-patterns.md (a prototype that departs from its design's R2 seam; a series rule that covers product and starter mutants but not the spec's own checks).

Time budget (O10): on this Mac the file takes 22.2-22.3 s (my sketch) and 22.0-22.2 s (the author's). By the design's own model the 30000 question line is crossed on the runner at a ratio of about 1.96 (REQ-105 saw 2.0 for the smoke file); the limit 50000 only at about 4.5. ORCH can expect the question to the owner at step 6 or 9; it is not a failure of the criterion.

A kit trap for TEST-DESIGNER: page.waitFor('() => <condition>') with no args evaluates the function expression itself, which is truthy, so the wait ends at once. My own sketch fell into it in two waits (mask, reconnect) and still passed until I fixed it; the design's mutant P05 would catch it in mask, and in reconnect the next wait covers it. Worth one line for TEST-DESIGNER (page code with args, or an expression, never a bare function without args) and a candidate for docs/anti-patterns.md.

Outside REQ-106: the hook stamps the time as its first action (hook.js line 12, REQ-001 criterion 2), but no test pins it: my V-P05 (the stamp taken after the input is read) survives the spec and all 50 tests of pixel-office-hook.test.js. Importance low (milliseconds), reproduce with the substitution in self_check.mutants. ORCH decides whether to open a defect.
